styles.name: linear-lr
styles.description: Hard-edge curtain sweeping left → right: a clean vertical wipe line advances from the left edge to the right as progress rises 0→1

styles.name: linear-tb
styles.description: Horizontal curtain dropping top → bottom: the revealed band grows downward one dot-row at a time as progress rises

styles.name: barn-door
styles.description: Barn-door wipe: the left half slides left and the right half slides right, parting from the vertical centre seam as progress rises

styles.name: iris
styles.description: Iris wipe: a filled circle expands from the grid's centre, its radius growing from zero to cover the full screen as progress reaches 1

styles.name: iris-diamond
styles.description: Diamond iris wipe: a filled rhombus expands from the centre using Manhattan (L1) distance — produces sharp 45° diamond edges instead of the circular iris's smooth curve

styles.name: diagonal
styles.description: Diagonal wipe: a 45° slanted edge sweeps from the top-left corner to the bottom-right, revealing the screen along the anti-diagonal axis

styles.name: checkerboard
styles.description: Checkerboard wipe: the screen is split into an alternating tile grid; even tiles fill first and odd tiles follow, creating a two-pass chequerboard dissolve as progress crosses 0.5

styles.name: venetian-blinds
styles.description: Venetian-blinds wipe: the screen is divided into horizontal slats; each slat opens symmetrically from its own centreline, all in unison, so the full height is revealed in parallel stripes

styles.name: dissolve
styles.description: Ordered Bayer-dither dissolve: each dot has a threshold from a 4×4 matrix; it lights up when progress exceeds its threshold, producing a structured stipple that expands uniformly across the screen

styles.name: clock-wipe
styles.description: Clock wipe: a radial pie slice rotates clockwise from 12 o'clock, sweeping the filled region around the centre like a clock hand until the full circle is revealed at progress 1

styles.name: spiral
styles.description: Archimedean spiral wipe: each dot is revealed according to its spiral parameter θ = √(r/r_max)·N_turns·2π, so the filled region uncoils outward from the centre in a continuous tight helix

styles.name: split
styles.description: Split wipe: two horizontal bands advance from the top edge and bottom edge simultaneously, meeting at the vertical midline when progress = 1

styles.name: zigzag
styles.description: Zigzag wipe: a left-to-right curtain whose leading edge is a sine wave, producing a rippling serrated boundary that sweeps across the screen

styles.name: pixelate
styles.description: Pixelate wipe: the screen is divided into coarse 2×1-cell blocks, each ramp from empty → ░ → ▒ → ▓ → █ as progress rises through four density thresholds — a block-density mosaic that fills by region, not by edge
